newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: SURGERY DELAYS IN NSW HOSPITALS TODAY
People wanting elective surgery in New South Wales public hospitals can expect delays today due to industrial action by doctors.

Doctors, interns, and resident medical officers are taking stop-work action to protest against Federal Government plans to restrict access to Medicare provider numbers, which could affect the careers of medical graduates.
Doctors will hold stopwork meetings in Sydney, Gosford, Newcastle, and Wollongong.
PASSENGERS ESCAPE PLANE CRASH UNINJURED
A light plane has crashed-landed in Western Australia near the Kimberley town of Derby.
The twin engine aircraft, with seven people on board, was on its way to a mining camp last night and had just taken off from the Derby airport when it ditched into a swamp.
The pilot suffered a nose injury but the six passengers escaped unhurt.
Police say the high tide prevented them from salvaging the aircraft.
The Bureau of Air safety is investigating the accident.
CONFIDENCE IN AVIATION AUTHORITY ERODING
There are growing doubts about the effectiveness of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority.
Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp, says public confidence in the authority is eroding, and questions are being asked if its board is adequately doing its job.
Mr Sharp has again written to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority raising concerns, following the crash of a Barrier Air plane on Sunday near Cairns.
CONTEMPT APPLICATION DENIED
The ACT Magistrates court has denied an application by the lawyer of the former Australian Ambassador to Cambodia to have a Cambodian teenager dealt with for contempt of court.
The boy claims he had sex with the former Ambassador on two occassions in Phnom Penh in 1994.
John Scott Holloway, 53, has been charged with having sex with a child under 16 years of age under the Child Sex Tourism Act.
He has not yet entered a formal plea.
Magistrate Michael Soames said he was reluctant to deal with the boy for contempt because of his age, and the length of time he'd spent in the witness box.
NO THREAT TO FISCHER: SENATOR
Speculation that the National Party leadership of Tim Fischer is under threat is being dismissed by Victorian Senator Julian McGauaran.

Senator McGauran says there's no meaningful dissent against the Deputy Prime Minister, despite reports some Queensland Nationals are unhappy with his ability to push the interests of the party in the Coalition.
Senator McGauran says that feeling won't lead to a challenge to Mr Fischer.
